paper_metadata.title: Quantum computing for multidimensional option pricing: End-to-end pipeline

summary: The paper proposes an end‑to‑end pipeline combining NIG‑based risk‑neutral density calibration with Quantum Amplitude Estimation for multidimensional option pricing. In simulator experiments (≈6 qubits), the quantum accelerated Monte Carlo estimator shows the expected scaling improvement from O(1/ε²) (classical Monte Carlo) to O(1/ε), with simulations suggesting roughly 10–100× fewer oracle queries for accuracies below about 10⁻³. All results are obtained on an ideal simulator using discretized toy instances.

experiments.description: Quantum accelerated Monte Carlo (QAMC) estimation of cosine-series coefficients for calibrated NIG marginal densities, compared against classical Monte Carlo, using the AXA 1-year expiry density as the main reported example.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Accelerated Monte Carlo using modified Real Quantum Amplitude Estimation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Square-root encoding of the discretized marginal density fi(xj) into amplitudes; one ancilla qubit used to encode the basis-function expectation via controlled rotation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate cosine coefficients a_k = E[gamma_k(X_i)] for the marginal density expansion f_i(x) ≈ sum_k a_k gamma_k(x).

problem_instance.description: Recovery of the AXA marginal risk-neutral density from market option quotes, then estimation of cosine-series coefficients for the density approximation.

dataset_specification.description: AXA options; 1-year expiry; market data as of 24/12/2024; closing spot price 33.8 EUR

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Calibrated NIG marginal from market quotes; cosine-series truncation on a finite interval; reference values computed by classical Riemann quadrature; 25 repeated trials.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Error convergence versus number of samples/queries; average over 25 repetitions; 90% confidence intervals reported.

implementation_details.classical_solver: classical Monte Carlo / classical Riemann quadrature baseline
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: NIG calibration from market quotes; cosine-basis setup; discretization with J=25 points and n=5 qubits per dimension.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Coefficient error computation against classical Riemann reference; averaging over 25 runs; confidence intervals.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: error decreases approximately as O(1/sqrt(L)) classically and O(1/epsilon) quantumly; QAMC shows quadratic advantage

results.unit: basis points (normalized by spot), maximum pricing error
basis points (around ATM strike, typical error)

speedup_claims.conditions: amplitude-estimation query model; coefficient recovery and pricing via QAE/QAMC
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports asymptotic O(1/epsilon) vs O(1/epsilon^2); no wall-clock timing or hardware execution on real QPU.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/epsilon) per amplitude-estimation query model; coefficient recovery uses O(sqrt(b_i-a_i) K_i^2 / epsilon_i log(K_i/rho_i)) queries

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not estimated; paper reports asymptotic O(1/epsilon) vs O(1/epsilon^2) scaling only.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires scalable fault‑tolerant implementation of amplitude estimation plus efficient state‑preparation oracle AX_i for probability distributions.
limiting_factors: Experiment executed on ideal simulator only
No hardware resource estimates for large‑scale implementation

notes: Hardware is the paper's quantum simulator environment (myQLM/NEASQC); no real QPU is named.
Num qubits inferred from J=25 discrete points => n=5 qubits per dimension and one ancilla, giving 6 total qubits.
Paper demonstrates asymptotic convergence behavior via simulation but no real hardware experiment or practical runtime comparison.

experiments.description: Quantum accelerated Monte Carlo pricing of a 2-asset spread call option under a Gaussian copula, comparing joint and independent formulations against classical Monte Carlo.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Accelerated Monte Carlo with joint and independent copula formulations; iterative quantum amplitude estimation for positive payoff

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Joint density loaded into amplitudes for the joint formulation; independent marginals plus copula-weighted payoff for the independent formulation.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate V(T,K)=e^{-rT}E[h(S,K)] for a spread option under a Gaussian-copula joint distribution.

problem_instance.description: 2-asset spread option pricing with AXA and Michelin as underlyings.

dataset_specification.description: AXA and Michelin; 1-year expiry; market data as of 24/12/2024

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Marginals calibrated with NIG; joint dependence modeled by Gaussian copula; marginal densities recovered classically with K=27 to isolate final pricing error; 25 repeated trials.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Error convergence versus samples/queries; average over repetitions with 90% confidence intervals; comparison of CMC, QAMC-joint, and QAMC-independent.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Gaussian-copula construction; NIG marginal calibration; classical Riemann-sum reference price; K=27 marginal recovery done classically.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Comparison of convergence curves for CMC and QAMC (joint and independent).

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: QAMC converges as O(1/epsilon) and CMC as O(1/epsilon^2); joint formulation has lower intercept than independent formulation

speedup_claims.conditions: 2-asset spread option pricing under Gaussian copula; QAMC with joint and independent formulations; iterative QAE for positive payoff
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper reports joint formulation has lower intercept than independent formulation; no explicit numeric price error values are stated in text.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(1/epsilon) for option-price estimation via QAE; paper also gives query bounds for joint/independent formulations

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not computed; authors only show asymptotic scaling plots.
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault‑tolerant QAE circuits with state‑preparation for joint or independent distributions; significantly larger qubit counts than the 6‑qubit toy setup.
limiting_factors: No full runtime comparison including classical preprocessing

notes: The paper explicitly states J=23 and n=6 qubits per dimension for the spread option, and total Nn=6 qubits for QAMC in the pricing experiments.
No transpiled depth or gate counts are reported.
Paper claims QAMC achieves quadratic improvement and empirically shows query scaling advantage versus CMC in simulation.
